android-settings.connect.deleteText: It disconnects from Slack. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

android-settings.connect.deleteTextSessi.other: It disconnects from Slack; the records of its {n} chats are kept but get no more messages. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

android-settings.connect.ownerNote: The owner decides whose “Mine” list the connect shows up in.
android-settings.connect.runtime: Runs on {runtime}, which can't change after creation; for another runtime, create a new connect. Ongoing chats keep the settings they started with.
android-settings.connect.slackAppNote: Changes are written straight to this app in Slack
android-settings.connects.empty: No connects on this machine yet

android-settings.flow.appToken: Generate an App-Level Token on the Socket Mode page and copy it (starts with xapp-; scopes are already chosen).
android-settings.flow.installManual: The app is ready. Install it to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (starts with xoxb-) on the OAuth page.
android-settings.flow.installOauth: The app is ready. Install it to the workspace: click “Allow” in Slack and the bot token goes to the station automatically.
android-settings.flow.manual: Build the app yourself, without a configuration token
android-settings.flow.manual1: Create a new app in Slack from {app}'s manifest.
android-settings.flow.manual2: Generate an App-Level Token on the app's Socket Mode page (scopes are already chosen).
android-settings.flow.manual3: Install it to the workspace on the Install App page and copy the Bot User OAuth Token.
android-settings.flow.manualInSlack: Build the app in Slack yourself, without a configuration token
android-settings.flow.noModels: No models are on in this station's profiles yet. Turn some on in the profiles on the station page first.
android-settings.flow.noProfileNote: A connect runs its model through a profile. Add one, then come back to add the connect.
android-settings.flow.permsNote: Permissions use the default (all on); change them later in the connect's “Slack app”.
android-settings.flow.removeTokenText: {app} will stop using it to build and edit apps in this Slack workspace. Apps and connects already made aren't affected; you can add it again later.
android-settings.flow.title: Add connect
android-settings.flow.tokenNote: With a Slack configuration token, {app} builds the app in Slack for you: fill in its name, icon and permissions here instead of setting each one up in Slack's admin pages. The token is yours alone.
android-settings.flow.whichTeam: Which Slack workspace's configuration token to build the app with.
android-settings.login.codexNote: On the OpenAI page, sign in with the ChatGPT account {app} should use and paste the code. This continues by itself when you're done. If the page says device code sign-in is off, turn it on in ChatGPT's security settings first.
android-settings.login.copyOpen: Copy code and open sign-in page
android-settings.login.manual: You can also sign in by hand on that machine
android-settings.login.note: Sign-in happens on the machine running {app}; you only authorize it in the browser.
android-settings.login.openPageRest: , sign in with the Claude account {app} should use, and agree.
android-settings.login.signedIn: Signed in. To switch accounts, sign in again.

android-settings.members.title: Members
android-settings.mode.back: Switching back to a single chat later picks up the original one.
android-settings.mode.keepSession: It picks up the single chat it was bound to before.
android-settings.mode.mention: From now on only threads where it's @-mentioned go into the chat; replies in threads already in still arrive.
android-settings.mode.mentionOff: Every message it can see in its channels goes into the chat.
android-settings.mode.mentionOn: Later replies in an @-mentioned thread don't need another @.
android-settings.mode.newSession: The next message starts a new single chat; you can also pick an existing chat after switching.
android-settings.mode.noMention: No @ needed: every message in all channels and DMs it can see goes to the agent, which uses noticeably more.
android-settings.mode.oldThreads: Threads that went on in the single chat need a new @ to continue, which opens a new chat without the earlier context.

android-settings.mode.running.one: 1 chat is running now; it finishes its current turn.
android-settings.mode.running.other: {n} chats are running now; they finish their current turn.

android-settings.mode.title: Chat mode
android-settings.mode.toMulti: The chat bound now gets no new messages. From now on, each thread opens its own new chat when @-mentioned.
android-settings.mode.toSingle: From now on, all its messages go into one chat; the existing per-thread chats get no new messages, including replies in those threads. Their records are kept.
android-settings.models.empty: Once the profile is checked, the models it can use are listed here; tick them to use them.
android-settings.models.note: Only ticked models can be chosen in new chats and connects.
android-settings.notify.on: When something's done, needs you, fails, or someone speaks
android-settings.notify.title: Notifications
android-settings.pickStation: Which station to add it on
android-settings.profile.background: Move running commands to the background when a new message arrives
android-settings.profile.backgroundOff: New messages are read only after the running command or subagent finishes.
android-settings.profile.backgroundOn: Commands and subagents keep running in the background, and the agent reads the message right away.
android-settings.profile.deleteText: Removes it from {app}'s settings only; its config directory and the login in it aren't deleted.
android-settings.profile.disableText: {app} stops using the {runtime} login on this machine. The login on the machine isn't affected, and you can use it again later.
android-settings.profile.fastNote: Chats that follow the subscription use this; Fast uses more allowance or credits
android-settings.profile.machineNote: To switch accounts, sign in again or sign out, do it in {runtime} on this machine and this profile follows. To stop using it, turn it off (menu at top right).
android-settings.profile.noUsers: No connects use this profile yet.
android-settings.profile.offline: {name} is offline; you can act once it reconnects
android-settings.profile.subscriptionNot: Sign-in happens on the machine running {app}; you only authorize it in the browser. The profile is added once sign-in succeeds.
android-settings.profiles.empty: No profiles on this machine yet
android-settings.profiles.note: The accounts agents run models with. Accounts that need a look come first on each station; open one to see why and how to fix it.
android-settings.profiles.stationOffline: Station offline; can't load its profiles
android-settings.quota.title: Allowance
android-settings.run.noModels: No models are on in the {runtime} profiles yet. Turn some on in the profiles on the station page first.

android-settings.run.saved: Saved; new chats will use the new settings
android-settings.run.title: Change model

android-settings.slack.group.dm.note: Open direct messages with one or more people.

android-settings.slack.updatedApprove: Updated. Takes effect once you approve the new permissions in Slack
